title: Best Indian Sports Films
description: Cricket, wrestling, boxing, chess — Indian films about the games we love.
intro: Sport on screen only works when the human story matters more than the trophy.

entries.why_it_ranks: Cricket becomes the vehicle for resistance, unity and self-respect in an epic that combines sport, history, drama and entertainment almost perfectly.
Shah Rukh Khan's Kabir Khan and the women's hockey team deliver perhaps Indian cinema's finest combination of sporting tension, teamwork and redemption.
Wrestling, family and gender expectations combine in an enormously effective sports drama with exceptionally convincing training and competition sequences.
A deaf and mute village boy dreaming of playing cricket for India gives the genre one of its most heartfelt underdog stories.
Pa. Ranjith makes boxing inseparable from community, politics, caste and identity while delivering outstanding fight sequences.
Cricket becomes the setting for a deeply emotional story about failure, fatherhood, dignity and one last attempt at redemption.
Farhan Akhtar's transformation and Milkha Singh's journey from trauma to elite athletics give the film tremendous emotional and physical energy.
The climactic cycle race works because the film first makes us care about Sanju's transformation from irresponsible teenager to determined competitor.
Women's cricket and a daughter's ambition intersect with farming distress, gender barriers and a touching father-daughter relationship.
Priyanka Chopra brings enormous commitment to the story of a world-class boxer balancing sport, motherhood and social expectations.
R. Madhavan and Ritika Singh give this boxing drama tremendous physical credibility and an excellent volatile coach-athlete relationship.
Anurag Kashyap uses boxing to explore caste, institutional corruption, romance and the politics surrounding Indian sport.
A young woman's cricket ambitions become intertwined with family, farming and the determination to succeed despite limited opportunity.
One of Hindi cinema's important early sports dramas, using football to explore mentorship, discipline and adolescent confidence.
Venkatesh and Ritika Singh give the Telugu adaptation of Irudhi Suttru considerable emotional force, particularly through the difficult coach-boxer relationship.
Hockey and the dream of representing independent India provide the foundation for a rousing historical sports drama.
Irrfan Khan is extraordinary as an elite athlete whose life moves tragically from sporting achievement toward rebellion and violence.
Cricket is approached not through international glory but through an ordinary man whose unrealized sporting dreams influence how he raises his son.
Football provides the connection between cultures in a warm, deeply human story about community, migration and unexpected family bonds.
Local cricket becomes a vehicle for rivalry, caste, friendship and social identity in an unusually grounded sports drama.
Field hockey gets a rare mainstream spotlight in an energetic commercial film about teamwork and protecting a community sporting ground.
Hockey, corruption and the commercialization of sporting institutions are wrapped inside an accessible mainstream entertainer.
Athletics becomes a vehicle for examining the difficult realities faced by young Indian athletes pursuing professional sport.
Basketball — rarely represented in Indian cinema — anchors a story about friendship, rivalry and the unequal attention given to different sports.
Football and history intersect in a dramatization of Mohun Bagan's famous 1911 IFA Shield victory, giving the list an important regional and historical dimension.
